params.forwarder_: The Chainlink KeystoneForwarder for the target chain
params.workflowName_: The CRE workflow name as bytes10 (0 to not enforce)
params.workflowOwner_: The CRE workflow owner address — the per-action {OspexCreTimelock} on a        governed mainnet deploy

params.jsonoddsId: External id from the JSONOdds API
params.rundownId: External id from the Rundown API
params.sportspageId: External id from the Sportspage API

onReport(bytes,bytes).details: If this function call reverts, it can be retried with a higher gas limit. The receiver is responsible for discarding stale reports.

requestMarketUpdate(uint256).details: Bumps the contest's market nonce. {onReport} then accepts a market report whose echoed nonce      is a real request (<= the latest) and not yet superseded by an applied report (>      s_lastAppliedMarketNonce) — so stale odds can't overwrite fresh ones, AND this permissionless      bump can't invalidate an in-flight legitimate report. Reverts unless the contest is Verified      (ContestModule re-checks on apply; this is a fast-fail).

params.contestId: The contest to refresh markets for

returns.requestNonce: The new latest market nonce for the contest

requestScore(uint256).details: Reverts unless the contest is Verified AND its start time has passed — scoring a game that      has not started is necessarily premature (the workflow would fail anyway, but we avoid      emitting known-premature, workflow-owner-funded requests). Score is one-shot at the      ContestModule, so it carries no nonce.

EVENT_ORACLE_REPORT_PROCESSED().notice: Core-hub event type for an applied DON report. Mirrors the native         {CreReportProcessed} through OspexCore so a single core-only subscription sees the         oracle report envelope (reportKey, requestType, applied nonce, workflow version) that         the ContestModule state events do not carry.

EVENT_ORACLE_REQUESTED().notice: Core-hub event type for a permissionless oracle request. Mirrors the native         {CreOracleRequested} through OspexCore so a core-only subscription sees the request         side too — market/score requests have no ContestModule event, and verify's request is         otherwise only inferable from CONTEST_CREATED. One uniform request stream, all 3 types.

createContestAndRequestVerify(string,str.notice: Permissionless. Creates a contest (Unverified) and emits a verify request that         the CRE workflow resolves. The caller pays the USDC contest-creation fee (charged         by ContestModule via OspexCore); the CRE workflow run itself is workflow-owner-funded.

i_forwarder().notice: The trusted Chainlink KeystoneForwarder — the only valid {onReport} caller

i_ospexCore().notice: The OspexCore contract (module registry + event hub)

i_workflowName().notice: The expected workflow name (bytes10). Enforced when non-zero. The workflow ID is         deliberately not pinned (CRE rotates it on every update).

i_workflowOwner().notice: The expected workflow owner. On a governed mainnet deploy this is the         per-action {OspexCreTimelock} timelock address.

requestMarketUpdate(uint256).notice: Permissionless. Emits a market-update request for an existing (Verified) contest. The         CRE workflow fetches current odds and writes them back via {onReport}.

requestScore(uint256).notice: Permissionless. Emits a score request for an existing (Verified) contest whose game has         started. The CRE workflow fetches the final scores and writes them back via {onReport}.

s_lastAppliedMarketNonce(uint256).notice: contestId → the highest market nonce already APPLIED by a report. A market report is         accepted only if its nonce is > this (and <= s_marketNonce). Comparing to the last         APPLIED nonce (not the latest REQUESTED) blocks stale overwrites while ensuring a cheap         permissionless {requestMarketUpdate} cannot invalidate an in-flight legitimate report.

s_marketNonce(uint256).notice: contestId → latest market-update request nonce (the highest REQUESTED). Bumped on every         {requestMarketUpdate}. A market report is accepted only if its echoed nonce is a real         request (<= this) and not yet superseded by an applied report (> s_lastAppliedMarketNonce).

s_processedReport(bytes32).notice: keccak256(report) → processed. Replay guard; reverts roll the flag back so a         first-delivery out-of-gas revert can be retried by the forwarder.

s_scoreRequested(uint256).notice: contestId → a score request was emitted for it (set in {requestScore}). {_handleScore}         is fail-closed on this, so an unrequested score report is rejected.

s_verifyRequested(uint256).notice: contestId → a verify request was emitted for it (set in {createContestAndRequestVerify}         when the contest is created). {_handleVerify} is fail-closed on this, so a verify report         for contest 0 / any uncreated, unrequested slot can never create a ghost Verified contest.
